Prior work shows that VLMs achieve higher accuracy on textual tasks compared to visual equivalents Frank et al. ( 2021 ); Fu et al. ( 2024 ); van Sprang et al. ( 2025 ) . This gap is attributed to distinct internal mechanisms for visual and textual processing Nikankin et al. ( 2025 ); Golovanevsky et al. ( 2025b ) and to modality-specific parametric knowledge Zhu et al. ( 2024 ) . VLMs also struggle to disentangle different signals, both across their input modalities Hua et al. ( 2025 ) and between their input and parametric knowledge Tang et al. ( 2023 ); Golovanevsky et al. ( 2025a ); Ortu et al. ( 2025 ) . Recent work investigated how VLMs perform under inconsistent or conflicting textual and visual inputs Yan et al. ( 2025 ); Zhao et al. ( 2025 ) . Given conflicting information, current VLMs tend to disproportionately prefer textual information Salin et al. ( 2022 ); Deng et al. ( 2025 ) , which can manifest in sycophantic behavior Pi et al. ( 2025 ) . Further exploring modality conflicts, Zhang et al. investigated modality preference through the lens of unimodal uncertainty. In contrast, our work studies modality conflicts stemming from minor, realistic inconsistencies and examines a more complex task that more closely reflects real-world usage.
